items.problem: The mandatory bootstrap self-check ran concurrently with initialization and initially returned False.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 94-103 show Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 and Test-Path issued together; the check completed before bootstrap.
items.covered_clearly_at: SKILL.md Step 0 numbers scaffold, bootstrap, and self-check as ordered commands and says not to proceed until Test-Path returns True.
items.why_no_skill_change: The order and required True result were already explicit; the agent reran the check successfully.

items.problem: The copied manifest retained missing UWP-branded image references and a launch raced the correcting rebuild.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 4340-4364 shows the manifest correction followed by a launch that still consumed stale Splash-sdk.png output.
items.covered_clearly_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md #csproj, 'Package.appxmanifest - reconcile image references with the assets you actually have', explicitly names Splash-sdk.png, 0x80073CF6, and requires Test-Path checks before first launch; Validate-UwpMigration also checks all image references.
items.why_no_skill_change: The existing section predicts the exact error and gives both valid fixes; following it before launch would prevent the failure.

items.problem: The first custom Program.cs build failed with CS0029 because '_ = new App()' assigned to a lambda parameter named underscore.
items.covered_clearly_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md #startup-crashes shows the custom entry-point shape and the trial's own compiler message identified the local type mismatch.
items.why_no_skill_change: This was ordinary C# variable shadowing, fixed immediately, and does not require migration-specific guidance.

items.problem: A rebuild and its dependent launch were issued concurrently, causing an incomplete-layout warning.
items.covered_clearly_at: SKILL.md Step 3 defined the loop as build then launch and presented the commands in that order.
items.why_no_skill_change: Build output must exist before any launcher can inspect it; the existing ordered workflow was sufficient, though the corrected command now makes the dependency even more explicit.
